messages:
jon: Heads up — saw customer report + internal repro where long-context sessions slowly leak KV memory and eventually return stale tokens across unrelated requests. Repro attached below, happening after a batch resume that switches kernels. Suspect token-alignment drift when pages are reused across batch boundaries.

maria: repro steps? logs?

jon: short repro: run long-chat-worker with --seq-len 12k and interleave small concurrent requests. After ~2000 tokens memory growth ~30MB and you start seeing tokens from previous session appearing in outputs.

jon: example command:
```
./long-chat-worker --model redwood/yy-13b --batch-size 4 --enable-kv-paging --kv-page-size 64k --kernel-prefer auto
# then send: session A: 12k tokens continuous
# session B: short Q&A bursts every 30s
```

jon: snippet from runtime log at contamination point:
```
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] KV_PAGE_REF tag=0x9b4a req=aa12 append_offset=488320 owner_session=4812
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] KV_PAGE_REF tag=0x9b4a req=bb33 append_offset=488320 owner_session=4820
[WARN] kv_cache: page 0x9b4a reused without clearing session_tag -> possible stale block served
```

anika: this smells like our resume path for split batches. kernel switch clears per-kernel append pointers but we only clear the page's last_written_offset when eviction/claim happens. If two kernels race to append and we reuse the same physical page ID but with different logical alignment, you can get token offsets shifted.

ryan: did perf tracing show extra memcpy or unexpected locks? I ran a perf trace on the repro run:
```
# perf top diff around regression window
- memcpy  +0.8%
- kv_cache_lock contend +1.5%
- page_table_walks +2.3%
```
ryan: also saw a bump in tail-latency (~95p +12ms) when the pager triggered while a batch resumed.

anika: likely root cause: reclaim path marks page free but doesn't atomically zero session_tag/owner_id before another request reclaims it. If batch A writes a partial fragment, then is preempted -> evict decision -> batch B reclaims same page, append_offset mismatch leads to misaligned KV reads.

maria: can we add an assert in debug builds that checks page.owner_session == current_session or page.valid_bytes == 0 before reuse?

jon: yes, added a local debug assert and repro fails fast. Patch idea: on reclaim, set page.owner_session = INVALID and page.valid_bytes = 0 under the eviction lock, then publish. Also add a scanning sanitiser that flags >1 session touch within page lifetime.

perf-bot: [perf-alert] kv-cache: memory growth detected in job long-chat-worker (canary) — 28MB over 1500s, associated with pager churn.

anika: short-term mitigation: disable kernel auto-switch for pager-enabled endpoints (force single kernel path) until fix lands. That avoids the cross-kernel reuse race.

ryan: I'll prototype a unit test that simulates interleaved reclaim + append across two logical kernels. Add it to eng-runtime/kv_cache_test.cc with 1000 randomized iterations.

jon: assigning: @anika to write reclamation patch + integration tests, @ryan to write unit fuzz test and perf regression case, @maria to run canary with kernel lock disabled across our fleet slice.

maria: running canary now (slice=kv-pager-e2e). Will report back in ~2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jon: thanks all. logging follow-ups: add a metric kv.page_reuse_without_clear and an alert if >5/min. That'll catch any remaining contamination in prod. :+1:
